source_note: Curated from US federal healthcare regulations (HIPAA, EMTALA, Stark, AKS). NOT derived from FAOS ontology blueprints (E1 anti-circularity).

requirements.requirement: Apply minimum necessary standard — use or disclose only the minimum PHI needed for the purpose
Obtain written patient authorization before disclosing PHI for purposes not covered by TPO exceptions
Provide patients right of access to their own PHI within 30 days of request
Implement technical safeguards: access controls, audit controls, integrity controls, transmission security
Notify affected individuals within 60 days of discovering a breach of unsecured PHI
Require Business Associate Agreements before sharing PHI with third-party service providers
Provide medical screening examination to any individual presenting at emergency department
Stabilize emergency medical condition before discharge or transfer
Ensure appropriate transfer with patient consent, physician certification, and receiving facility acceptance
Prohibit physician self-referral for designated health services unless an exception applies
Verify applicable Stark Law exceptions (in-office ancillary, fair market value, etc.) before referral
Do not offer or receive remuneration to induce referrals for services covered by federal healthcare programs
Verify applicable safe harbors (employee, personal services, warranties, etc.) for any financial arrangement
Obtain informed consent including risks, benefits, and alternatives before procedures
Maintain complete and accurate medical records for each patient
Apply standardized triage scoring system to prioritize patients by acuity level
Track and report core quality measures: readmission rates, mortality rates, patient satisfaction
Retain HIPAA-related documentation for minimum 6 years from date of creation or last effective date
Comply with CMS Conditions of Participation for Medicare-certified facilities
Report patient safety events to Patient Safety Organization without retaliation
Only licensed practitioners may prescribe controlled substances with proper DEA registration
Base clinical recommendations on current evidence-based guidelines and clinical protocols
Calculate hospital-acquired infection rates and compare against national benchmarks
Monitor emergency department wait times and door-to-provider time against benchmarks
Ensure accurate coding and billing — do not upcode, unbundle, or submit claims for services not rendered
